piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:77, Op.76 No.3 (“Emperor”)
piece.movement: II. Poco adagio; cantabile — Var. II
piece.why: Variation II: the hymn moves to the cello while Violin I plays a busy countermelody above it. Both planners mislabel the violin as the tune here; the cello's hymn is still kept.

roster.label: Quartet that lost its viola: 2 violins, cello, + a clarinet

plan.summary: This is a straight one-to-one quartet cover. The Violin 1 tune stays on the advanced violin. Violin 2's inner line stays on the second violin. The viola's low pedal-note bass goes to the cello, and the clarinet takes the cello's singing tenor counterline. In the last bar the cello takes the cello part's low G2, which is below the clarinet's range, so the piece ends on a solid low G, while the clarinet fills in the viola's G3.

assignments.reason: The main tune, with fast sixteenth-note runs up to D6. It suits the advanced violinist and fits the range as written.
A mid-register inner harmony line (G3–C5) that fits the second violin exactly. The few double stops in bars 48–51 are simple and can be kept.
The viola's sustained D pedal is the lowest line here, so it is the bass. Cello plays it in its own range, and it reaches down to C3, which is too low for the clarinet.
The cello's moving tenor counterline (F#3–G4), including scale runs. The clarinet's agile, warm chalumeau register fits it well, and it stays above the cello's bass.
The final cadence: G3 dropping to low G2. Only the cello can reach this, so the cello finishes the bass.
The viola's last G3 fills out the final chord. The clarinet is free once the cello takes over the bass.
